posts.name: BlueHairedMeerkat
posts.cooked:
PeterCHayward:

@BlueHairedMeerkat: What's the story behind your username?

Many (like, five?) years ago, in the heyday of my youth, I wrote an incredibly short-lived webcomic about a fictionalised version of me and my friends playing board games in an attic during the zombie apocalypse, in which my character had blue hair. A friend of mine drew the thing and posted it on deviantArt. I wanted to reply to a comment on one of them - this meant I needed a deviantArt account, and chose Blue-Hair because of the comic. Given that I didn't really have a dominant username at that point, I started using Blue-Hair, but there are only so many times you can read the words 'Blue-Hair is already taken. Choose another username' before you think 'You know, maybe I should change this'. I genuinely don't remember where Meerkat came from, but it's been there ever since (except for in places with overly-restrictive character limits, where I'm BlueHairedKat or BlueMeerkat or some other variant).

I do not have blue hair. My hair right now is a fetching shade of orange.

Ameena:

[…] UXM266 - If you could meet up with any fictional character and have a chat with them, whom would you meet and what would you talk to them about/ask them?

This is a good question. As of now, it's probably Superman. I am fan of Superman, especially the stories that don't necessarily star him, but are about him. I would love to meet up with him and discuss what he thinks a superhero should be, and what he thinks about the current state of the world. I want to ask him about his sheer optimism, his morality, and his role as a hero. What he thinks the role the Justice League plays in respect to organizations such as the military and the police force. I'd also like to discuss what he thinks heroes (both anti, and basic) should do. Should they interact with the public? What type of feeling should, we as common folk, should feel when we hear or see them? I want to know what he thinks is important for his country its allies. I'd like to discuss his role working in the media, as both being a popular story, and a writer of said stories. How does he keep his biases in check? What stories does he think should be reported? I don't want to be judgemental, I want it to be very much like "My Dinner with Andre". Philosophy, communication, ideology, and semiotics.

 

@Trajector: In the past spy movies, westerns, and cyberpunk dystopias were all the rage, and ahd thier time in the limelight. Currently superhero movies now seem to be the big new thing for movies and television. What do you think the next big trend will be?

posts.name: Trajector
posts.cooked:
UXM266:

@Trajector: In the past spy movies, westerns, and cyberpunk dystopias were all the rage, and ahd thier time in the limelight. Currently superhero movies now seem to be the big new thing for movies and television. What do you think the next big trend will be?

That’s really tough! I suppose if I get it right, I ought to be a movie producer…or at least an investor!

I think a few possibilities are reasonable. New sci-fi films and TV seem to be having a bit of a resurgence: Edge of Tomorrow, The Expanse, etc…so we could be looking at a new era in screen science fiction. But maybe a better idea is that studios are going to look for something to fill the void left when Game of Thrones ends after its eighth season. We’ll see a resurgence of historical/fantastical dramas, based in any time period or location that seems fresh: ancient Egypt, medieval France, Temeraire’s Europe, what have you. Prepare for lots more gritty, sexy sword play on TV.

And if I’m right, you’ll all fund my pitch, right?

That said, I love them both, I just have other decks I love more! And I still end up playing Legacy almost every time I sit down, just because I'm so often teaching (or just running complicatedly) the game and Legacy is such an easy autopilot and helps make the game be more successful more often. He's nowhere near my favorite, but he's definitely the only deck I can basically sleep-play without a thought. I could probably write a pretty straightforward computer code to predict order of priority based on cards in play and cards in hand at this point and just have a computer automate my play of Legacy.
